standard.title: Propose actions or responses
standard.description: propose actions or responses to an issue or challenge that consider possible effects of actions
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S06): Students considered effects of actions before proposing them and developed action plans with persuasive justification.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students propose actions or responses to environmental, local government or cultural issues, considering effects and forecasting futures.

nodes.label: Forecasting probable and preferred futures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can forecast a probable future and a preferred future for an issue and explain the difference between them.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one probable future and one preferred future for a specific issue and explain one action that could shift from the probable to the preferred.
nodes.typical_width: Forecast probable and preferred futures for environmental, local government or cultural issues (e.g. ocean plastics, habitat loss); identify resources needed; forecast outcomes of actions.
wider: Develop a detailed preferred future scenario for an issue with a multi-step action plan
Evaluate the realism of a preferred future scenario by identifying what would need to change to achieve it
nodes.hinge_reason: The probable/preferred future distinction is new at Year 4 — without it, proposals are wishes rather than evidence-based interventions.

response_modes.reason: Probable vs preferred future requires students to distinguish what IS likely from what SHOULD happen — explicitly contrast the two before expecting students to reason across them.

success_criteria: Describes a probable future for an issue
Describes a preferred future and identifies what would need to change to achieve it

nodes.label: Responsible decision-making and action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on personal behaviours, identify attitudes that affect their environment and propose awareness-raising strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one personal behaviour that affects the environment and propose one change to that behaviour.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on personal behaviours affecting the environment at local or global level; identify resources needed for proposed actions; propose solutions to waste management, endangered species protection or cultural issues; participate in cooperative decision-making.
wider: Develop an awareness-raising strategy for a specific environmental issue, including identifying the audience, the message and the medium
Evaluate whether a proposed action would genuinely achieve its goal and revise it if needed

response_modes.reason: Responsible decision-making integrates reflection, forecasting, effect analysis and communication — the full Year 4 civic and evaluating capability.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one personal behaviour affecting the environment
Proposes a specific action or awareness-raising strategy with a reason
